paragraphs.text: DKB CBS – QCB liquidity reporting. Prepared for DKB Finance, 21 October 2026.
Mapping reviewed: LCR & NSFR (Solo) Mapping.xlsx: 22 sheets; the rules sit mainly on LCR_00 and NSFR_00, with supporting tables LCR_01–17 and NSFR_01–04.
Balances: CAL extract (CONSOLIDATE.ASST.LIAB) at 31 Aug 2026, UAT, used to test whether the rules reach the balances that exist.
Reference: DKB customer sector codes: Retail 1000–1999, 4000–4004, 6000/6001, 7000/7001; Corporate 2000–2003, 2006, 4005, 5001, 5002; Government 2005; Banks & FI 2004.
Caveat. Findings are based on the rules as written. Amounts are indicative UAT figures showing the size of balances a rule does or does not reach; they are not reconciled report values.
All open term deposits and loans fall into the shortest buckets; drives both the LCR outflows/inflows and the NSFR
Retail deposits filtered by INDUSTRY instead of SECTOR (B1)
About 69bn of about 101bn retail-sector deposits (31 Aug) would be excluded
About 2.8bn of reserves (31 Aug) missing from HQLA and from NSFR central bank reserves
About 25bn of guarantees held as CONTDB/CONTDBBL missed in "other guarantees"; LCR and NSFR differ
Unclear which rule is implemented; NBS01/NBS001 issues flow into LCR and NSFR
Maturity condition is reversed: "(System Date − MATURITY.DATE) <= 30 days" (or <= 365 days)
LCR_00 C50, C51, C53, C54 (term deposits, "ADD" clause), C86, C87 (loan inflows); NSFR_00 C13, C14
Every open contract has a negative value and lands in the shortest bucket; the ">30 days" lines only catch contracts that matured more than 30 days ago
Use (MATURITY.DATE − System Date), as already done in LCR_00 C9 and NSFR_00 C22
Installments receivable are selected by the arrangement's final maturity date
Installments due within 30 days on longer financing are excluded; the full balance of financing maturing within 30 days is included
Use the installments scheduled within 30 days (payment schedule); DKB Finance to confirm
Retail deposits are filtered on INDUSTRY = 1000–1999, 4000–4004, which are sector codes
Of about 101bn retail-sector deposits (31 Aug), only about 32bn meet the INDUSTRY condition
Sector 2004 (banks and financial institutions) is included in non-financial lines
LCR_00 C86 (includes 2004, while C87 is 2004 only); NSFR_00 C17, C18 (corporate funding)
Financial institutions counted twice in LCR inflows; treated as corporate funding in NSFR
Small at 31 Aug (deposits about 0.2m outside the lists) but structurally incomplete
Use the full DKB sector code list
QCB reserves are selected from categories 5003 and 5004
LCR_00 C8 (Required Reserves), C9; NSFR_00 C30 (All Central bank reserves)
No balances in 5003/5004 at 31 Aug; the reserve sits in 18060/18061 (about 2.8bn, debit). HQLA and NSFR reserves reported as zero
Claims on and installments from central banks use category 5002
Confirm the categories with DKB Finance
Guarantee balance types differ between LCR and NSFR, and one type does not exist
Payment guarantees (28005): LCR_00 C72 CONTDBBL; NSFR_00 C58 CONTCR & CONTDRBL (note: "update with CONTDBBL"). Other guarantees: LCR_00 C73 and NSFR_00 C59 CONTCR & CONTDRBL
CONTDRBL does not exist in CAL. Guarantees in 28000–28999 are held as CONTDB/CONTDBBL (about 25.2bn at 31 Aug); only CONTCR (about 31m) is picked up in "other guarantees"
Use the same existing contingent type in both reports (CONTDB or CONTDBBL, to confirm)
Letters of credit and acceptances depend on Table 613 and on named ranges from another mapping
LCR_00 C74, C75; NSFR_00 C60 ("Table 613 Not available"; *LCTYPEBL, *LCLIAB next to an explicit list)
Unclear which list applies; dependency on a table that is not available
Keep one explicit list of LC and acceptance types in this mapping; confirm the 30-day expiry logic
Many lines hold two definitions: a formula referencing NBS01/NBS001 cells and a separate CAL or ECB rule
Unclear which is implemented; where NBS references are used, NBS01/NBS001 issues flow into LCR and NSFR
Keep one definition per line; if NBS references are kept, sequence the fixes after NBS01/NBS001
"All other assets" is derived from NBS01 total assets
NBS01 currently reports cash and other assets as zero (both runs), so the residual is wrong
Depends on the NBS01 corrections; reconcile to the trial balance
Deposit balance types include a non-existent type and miss matured deposits
LCR_00 C50–C58; NSFR_00 C13–C21: CREDIT, CURACCOUNT, CURBALANCE
CURBALANCE does not exist in CAL; PAYACCOUNT (about 340m at 31 Aug) not selected
LCR_00 C68 (derivatives manual, Table 620 dropped); NSFR_03, NSFR_04, LCR_12_1, LCR_12_2, LCR_15–17 marked "not reported by the bank"
Scope not documented in one place
DKB Finance to confirm and document the manual and out-of-scope items
Cash uses categories 10000–10025 and 12900–12919, consistent with the other reports.
Term deposits (6600–6999) are covered through the second ("ADD") clause of the deposit rules.
LCR_00 C9 and NSFR_00 C22 already use the correct maturity direction and can serve as the template for A1.
Treasury positions are read from the TMS outbound tables (CRSSUKKUK, CRSTBILLST, CRSMMDEALST), as in NBS01/NBS001.
DKB Finance to confirm A2 (installment logic), the sector codes for B1–B3, the contingent type for D1 and the scope items in E4.
SL to correct A1, B1, C1, D1 and E3 first; then the remaining items.
Agree for each line whether the NBS reference or the CAL rule applies (E1), and sequence after the NBS01/NBS001 corrections.
Rerun LCR and NSFR and reconcile HQLA (cash, QCB reserves) and the deposit outflows to the trial balance at the same date.
